reviews.text:
When i asked Google AI:
"Do inbox adverts violate GDPR"
It's response was!

Yes, certain inbox advertisements can violate the GDPR. Specifically, if an advertisement is displayed in a user's email inbox in a way that resembles an email and is used for direct marketing purposes, it is considered direct marketing under EU law and requires consent. The European Court of Justice has ruled on this, stating that if the advertisement is designed to resemble an email and is displayed within a user's inbox, it falls under the rules of direct marketing and therefore requires user consent.

Another issue,
Outlook often highlights the wrong email in the deleted folder while reading another, hitting delete thinking you are deleting the email you are reading actually delete the incorrectly highlight one, resultining in having to recover all the deleted emails in order to find it again.

Come on micro$oft, you used to write good software what has happened?, financial greed?.

reviews.title: Need unread view across all folders
reviews.text: If you create folders and rules to move specific messages to folders, you do so to stay organized and keep your inbox easier to manage. I understand rules can be created to override folder move rules, but this isn’t foolproof and does not catch all urgent messages. It also defeats the purpose of setting up folders in the first place.

reviews.title: Remove the ads at the top!!!
reviews.text:
You need to remove the ads at the top, or adjust the timing of when it appears after opening the app, or make it look far less similar to a regular email!!!

Currently, the ad’s position, appearance, and the timing of when it shows up in the email list are seriously causing users to tap on it by accident rather than intentionally. 

If this design is in purpose, then yes I’m honestly speechless. And I’m also pretty sure this won’t be the lowest rating you’ll receive here, especially since none of the other major email providers, such as Gmail or iCloud, have ads like this in their apps.

Although the subscription fee is only $2.99 per month, you know this isn’t really about the money. It’s about the level of care and respect that you show your loyal users.

reviews.title: Terrible Experience
reviews.text:
When it works it is good, it’s a boring adjective but there’s nothing remarkable about outlook which is why it is not worth the hassle in my opinion. 

I don’t go looking for an email app with flashy features, I look for an email app which does the job and can be relied upon. Outlook is certainly not that. On many occasions I return to my laptop/desktop/phone to use outlook for the simple endeavour of writing a quick email or accessing a OTP but no, Outlook has logged me out and insists I run around in circles; 
first to my browser to sign into microsoft, 
then to my outlook app,
diverted back to my browser to sign into microsoft again,
back to Outlook again and after all that… it’s still not working,
so I close the app and try again,
I find myself in the same loop.

What should have been a 1 minute task has turned into a 20 minute ordeal to access my account even when my passwords were accepted, it’s like a cashier accepting my tender but refusing the sale, like a bouncer accepting my credentials but refusing me entry.

Just to top it off, it refused to uninstall even after my computer told me it was ‘uninstalling’ which is in keeping with the whole experience. All in all, the user experience was Sisyphean, an exercise in futility and I would not recommend.
